## Summary

Add native text generation for the LFM3 family in SGLang.

| Model | Inputs | Output |
| --- | --- | --- |
| LFM3 | Text | Text |
| LFM3-VL | Text, images, video | Text |
| LFM3-Audio | Text, audio | Text |
| LFM3-Omni | Text, images, audio, video, including video soundtracks | Text |

Uses stock Transformers with `--trust-remote-code` to load the checkpoint-provided configs and processors.

## Implementation

- Shared LFM3 backbone with gated short convolutions, full/sliding-window attention, and SGLang's hybrid cache integration. Includes CuTe DSL convolution kernels and a PyTorch fallback.
- Vision and audio encoders, projectors, and checkpoint loading. Omni reuses these components and the text backbone.
- Multimodal preprocessing uses the checkpoint's Transformers processors and chat template. Omni supports mixed inputs and video/audio interleaving.
- FlashInfer defaults to paged prefill for correct sliding-window attention.

## Usage

Choose a checkpoint for the input modalities you need:

| Model | Checkpoint |
| --- | --- |
| Text | [LiquidAI/LFM3-1.7B](https://huggingface.co/LiquidAI/LFM3-1.7B) |
| Vision | [LiquidAI/LFM3-VL-2B](https://huggingface.co/LiquidAI/LFM3-VL-2B) |
| Audio | [LiquidAI/LFM3-Audio-2B](https://huggingface.co/LiquidAI/LFM3-Audio-2B) |
| Omni | [LiquidAI/LFM3-Omni-2B](https://huggingface.co/LiquidAI/LFM3-Omni-2B) |

For example, launch Omni:

```bash
sglang serve \
  --model-path LiquidAI/LFM3-Omni-2B \
  --trust-remote-code \
  --reasoning-parser auto --tool-call-parser auto \
  --served-model-name lfm3 \
  --port 30000
```

Send requests through `/v1/chat/completions`. This client works with each model; select supported content below. Replace example media URLs with files reachable by the server.

```python
import base64
from pathlib import Path
from openai import OpenAI

client = OpenAI(base_url="http://localhost:30000/v1", api_key="EMPTY")

def ask(content, **kwargs):
    response = client.chat.completions.create(
        model="lfm3",
        messages=[{"role": "user", "content": content}],
        temperature=0,
        max_tokens=256,
        **kwargs,
    )
    print(response.choices[0].message.content)

# Text
ask("What is the capital of Poland?")

# Image
image = {"type": "image_url", "image_url": {"url": "https://your-host/image.jpg"}}
ask([image, {"type": "text", "text": "Describe this image."}])

# Video
video = {"type": "video_url", "video_url": {"url": "https://your-host/video.mp4"}}
ask([video, {"type": "text", "text": "Describe this video."}])

# Audio
encoded = base64.b64encode(Path("question.wav").read_bytes()).decode("ascii")
audio = {"type": "input_audio", "input_audio": {"data": encoded, "format": "wav"}}
ask([audio, {"type": "text", "text": "Answer the spoken question in text."}])

# Omni: image + spoken question
ask([image, audio])

# Omni: video with its soundtrack
ask(
    [video, {"type": "text", "text": "Summarize what happens and what is said."}],
    extra_body={"use_audio_in_video": True},
)
```

For transcription, launch LFM3-Audio and call the existing endpoint:

```bash
curl http://localhost:30000/v1/audio/transcriptions \
  -F model=lfm3 -F file=@question.wav
```

## Validation

Validation below was run on development checkpoints. FP16, TP1, H100, FlashInfer against Transformers; serving uses stock Transformers 5.19.0 with `--trust-remote-code`.

| Suite | Prefill/decode checks | ROUGE-L |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Text | 4/4 | 4/4 |
| Vision | 16/16 | 14/16 |
| Audio → text | 5/5 | 5/5 |
| Omni → text | 22/22 | 20/22 |

All 211 targeted CPU tests and 259 subtests passed. Live tool calling with both parsers set to `auto` and startup rejection probes passed. Vision ROUGE compares raw output with parsing disabled.

Triton also passed all 20 text/vision prefill and decode checks in FP16 on H100 with 1,024-token prefill chunks, including a long prompt beyond the 256-token sliding window. All generated outputs matched the FlashInfer run; the same two vision ROUGE failures remained. Audio and Omni were not tested with Triton.

Additional coverage: BF16 Omni smoke tests on H100; independent BF16 text/VL validation on H200, including TP2 text.

### sm120 (consumer Blackwell) check: LFM3-1.7B-NVFP4 text on an RTX 5060

Setup: RTX 5060 8 GB (sm120), CUDA 13.3, torch 2.14.1+cu130, flashinfer 0.7.2, checkpoint `LiquidAI/LFM3-1.7B-NVFP4`, text only. Tested b05dd4a01f, then the conv kernel/tests from b1637c242a.

**1. Conv prefill race: reproduced on sm120, and b1637c242a fixes it**

Harness: fixed random inputs, relaunch `gated_causal_conv1d_prefill` (chunk=256, `has_initial_state`=1) 5000 times per case, compare bit-exact against a torch reference.

| batch (requests x tokens) | b05dd4a01f wrong launches | b1637c242a wrong launches |
|---|---:|---:|
| 7 x 257 | 0 / 5000 | 0 / 5000 |
| 31 x 257 | 4 / 5000 | 0 / 5000 |
| 64 x 257 | 5 / 5000 | 0 / 5000 |
| 128 x 257 | 10 / 5000 | 0 / 5000 |
| 16 x 300 | 0 / 5000 | 0 / 5000 |

In failing launches the final state still matched the reference and only early outputs were wrong (max abs error 6 to 11 in a small-chunk variant of the same harness), which matches the chunk-0 read / last-chunk write path. A 2048-token prefill chunk (the default here) fits at most 7 requests of 257+ tokens, and 7 x 257 never failed, so small GPUs rarely hit it; batches sized for 8k+ prefill chunks do.

We arrived at the same snapshot fix independently; b1637c242a's version is functionally identical. The updated kernel suite passes on sm120 (31/31).

Suggestion: `test_cute_prefill_across_chunk_boundary_with_initial_state` is one launch with two requests, so it checks the multi-chunk math but not the race: against the pre-fix kernel it passed 300/300 runs. A slow-marked case with many >256-token requests (e.g. 128 x 257, a few thousand launches, bit-exact) would guard against regressions.

**2. Idle-CTA grid cost (open item from round 2), measured on sm120**

Same b1637c242a kernel, dim 2048, K 7, bf16. The current grid (`n_chunks` from total T, times B) is compared with a grid sized by the longest request (`chunk >= T`, identical per-CTA work while every request is at most 256 tokens). Times are GPU-only, from CUDA-graph replay, per call:

| batch | CTAs (current / ideal) | current | ideal | extra per forward (13 conv layers) |
|---|---:|---:|---:|---:|
| 8 x 256 | 1,024 / 128 | 127.0 us | 125.9 us | 0.02 ms |
| 64 x 32 | 8,192 / 1,024 | 103.7 us | 100.6 us | 0.04 ms |
| 128 x 16 | 16,384 / 2,048 | 116.6 us | 112.9 us | 0.05 ms |
| 256 x 8 | 32,768 / 4,096 | 147.0 us | 140.9 us | 0.08 ms |
| 128 x 128 | 131,072 / 2,048 | 759.1 us | 723.2 us | 0.47 ms |

So on sm120 the idle CTAs cost 1 to 5% of the conv kernel, under 0.1% of a prefill forward at these sizes, since early-exit CTAs are cheap. It is still worth bounding `n_chunks` by the longest extend length (already on the host via `extend_seq_lens_cpu`, so no device sync), but it does not look urgent.

**3. NVFP4 on sm120 works; parity with the HF reference**

- Loads as `modelopt_fp4`. The default `--fp4-gemm-backend` on sm120 is `flashinfer_cutlass` (W4A4), which works; `flashinfer_cudnn` and `marlin` (W4A16) also work.
- Model-code parity: with the NVFP4 weights unpacked to BF16, SGLang matches the checkpoint's `modeling_lfm3.py` in Transformers. Top-1 agreement is 97 to 100% on prompts up to 3000 tokens, and greedy outputs are identical for 32 tokens on all prompts, including 5.9k-token prompts (three prefill chunks across the 256-token window). Radix/mamba prefix-cache hits reproduce cold logprobs exactly.
- W4A4 serving, `sglang.benchmark.serving` with random token ids:

| scenario | flashinfer_cutlass | flashinfer_cudnn |
|---|---:|---:|
| 1 user, 512 in / 256 out: median TPOT | 5.25 ms (184 tok/s) | 5.64 ms (172 tok/s) |
| 8 users, 1024 / 256: output tok/s | 1082 | 1056 |
| 32 users, 1024 / 256: output tok/s | 2776 | 2741 |
| 4 users, 4096 in / 8 out: input tok/s | 21.3k | 21.4k |

**4. Launch command on the NVFP4 model card**

The card uses `--reasoning-parser qwen3-thinking`. With it, any request with `chat_template_kwargs: {"enable_thinking": false}` returns an empty `content`, and the whole answer lands in `reasoning_content`. For example, "What is 12 + 30?" gives `content=''` and `reasoning_content='12 + 30 = 42\n\n42'`. `--reasoning-parser auto`, as used in this PR's description, handles both modes; it may be worth aligning the card.

**5. Minor, non-blocking**

LFM3 isn't registered as hybrid-SWA (`hybrid_swa=False`), so the 5 sliding-window layers keep full-context KV. That is correct, but only 6 of the 11 attention layers need full context, so a SWA pool would save about 45% of KV memory, which matters on 8 GB cards. Possibly a follow-up.

Follow-up with BF16 vs NVFP4 numbers on the same RTX 5060 (sm120), PR at b05dd4a01f, `--cuda-graph-max-bs-decode 32`:

| | BF16 (`LFM3-1.7B`) | NVFP4 W4A16 (`--fp4-gemm-backend marlin`) | NVFP4 W4A4 (default `flashinfer_cutlass`) |
|---|---:|---:|---:|
| 1 user decode, median TPOT | 9.16 ms | 5.41 ms | 5.25 ms |
| 32 users, 1024 in / 256 out: output tok/s | 1,570 | 1,832 | 2,776 |
| prefill, 4 x 4096 tokens: input tok/s | 9.9k | 9.8k | 21.3k |
| GSM8K chat (1319 q, thinking on, greedy, 2048-token cap) | 89.5% | 87.6% | 86.8% |
| answers finished within the cap | 92.5% | 91.1% | 90.0% |
| accuracy on finished answers | 96.7% | 96.1% | 96.4% |

So W4A4 is the right default on sm120: about 1.7x BF16 for decode and 2.2x for prefill. At this cap the GSM8K gap comes mostly from more reasoning traces running past 2048 tokens rather than from wrong final answers (W4A4 vs BF16 paired: 64 vs 28 discordant questions). That may be worth a note on the NVFP4 card.

Separately, for anyone serving more than 32 concurrent requests on small cards: raising `--cuda-graph-max-bs-decode` from 32 to 64 doubled W4A4 throughput at 64 users (1.56k to 3.26k tok/s). That is general tuning, not a PR issue.

## Test report: LFM3-1.7B on consumer GPU (RTX 4060 Laptop 8 GB, SM89/Ada, WSL2) — works end-to-end

Tested head `b1637c242a0ed7cf6575bab44a21a1be30a5b19a`. The native `Lfm3ForCausalLM` loads, captures CUDA graphs and generates coherent output; a separate pure-HF BF16 control also generated coherent output. **Go ahead from my side** — details below, including one suggestion for a cryptic failure mode we hit with a hand-quantized checkpoint.

### Environment

- GPU: RTX 4060 Laptop 8 GB (SM89, Ada), WSL2
- torch 2.14.1+cu130, torchvision 0.29.0+cu130 (matching the PR's `torch==2.14.1` pin)
- transformers 5.21.0, `flashinfer_python[cu13]` 0.7.2, `sglang-kernel` 0.4.10 (per `python/pyproject.toml`)
- Install: `uv pip install --no-deps "sglang @ git+https://github.com/tugot17/sglang@lfm3#subdirectory=python"` with `SGLANG_BUILD_RUST_EXTS=none` (no Rust toolchain on this box; the text-only path does not appear to need the Rust extensions) — built and installed cleanly.

### Checkpoint and serving setup

- `LiquidAI/LFM3-1.7B` manually quantized selected linear weights to per-tensor FP8 e4m3 with dynamic activation scaling (`weight_block_size: null`, neuralmagic-style `quant_method: "fp8"`). Kept in bf16: embeddings, `lm_head`, all norms, and the depthwise conv kernels.
- `--quantization fp8 --kv-cache-dtype fp8_e4m3`, 32k context, TP=1, CUDA graphs on.

### Results

- **Loads and serves correctly.** A short greedy smoke test produced coherent text. A separate BF16 Hugging Face control also produced coherent text; this was not a token-by-token comparison or comprehensive correctness validation.
- **CUDA graph capture succeeds** on the native implementation. One graph-enabled request generated 200 tokens in 2.34 s end-to-end (~85 output tokens/s including prefill and HTTP overhead). An earlier graph-disabled 150-token request took about 9.1 s end-to-end; these were not matched benchmark runs and do not establish a speedup.
- The server was configured for 32k context and FP8 KV cache; only short prompts were exercised, not a 32k-context test.

### Issue found: unquantized `self_attn.gate_proj` → cryptic load error

With a checkpoint whose `quantization_config` does not ship `ignored_layers`, `self_attn.gate_proj` (the 16×2048 attention out-gate) is instantiated as an FP8 linear while the checkpoint ships it in bf16, and loading fails with:

```
ValueError: Downcasting not allowed: target.dtype=torch.float8_e4m3fn,
loaded_weight.dtype=torch.bfloat16
```

We traced this via a `load_weights` wrapper to `model.layers.N.self_attn.gate_proj.weight`. Checkpoint-side fix that works:

```json
"quantization_config": {
  "quant_method": "fp8",
  "activation_scheme": "dynamic",
  "fmt": "e4m3",
  "weight_block_size": null,
  "ignored_layers": ["lm_head", "self_attn.gate_proj"]
}
```

Two notes that cost us some time:

1. The ignored-layer matcher is dotted-boundary substring matching (`_module_path_match`), **not** glob — `"*.self_attn.gate_proj"` silently does not match; plain `"self_attn.gate_proj"` does.
2. This is consistent with the official `LiquidAI/LFM3-1.7B-NVFP4` checkpoint, which excludes `self_attn*` per attention layer from quantization — i.e. Liquid themselves ship the attention gates (and attention projections) unquantized.

Suggestion: consider auto-ignoring `self_attn.gate_proj` for LFM3 (or at least raising a clearer error that names the offending module and hints at `ignored_layers`), so hand-quantized checkpoints don't trip over this.

### Context: fallback path is not viable (reinforces this PR)

Before testing the PR we tried the `TransformersForCausalLM` fallback on an older build (0.5.6.post3.dev10571): LFM3 loads and runs there, but generation is corrupted garbage in our attempts with official NVFP4 and manual FP8. The root cause was not isolated; hybrid cache handling is a hypothesis, not a confirmed diagnosis. CUDA graph capture also fails in the fallback. A separate BF16 pure-HF control produced coherent text, but did not test those quantized checkpoints outside SGLang. For anyone on older builds: don't bother with the fallback for LFM3; this PR is what makes it work.

### Verdict

Native implementation verified on SM89 with FP8 weights + FP8 KV cache + CUDA graphs, coherent short-prompt output, preliminary single-stream performance for a 1.7B on an 8 GB card. Thanks for the thorough PR — text-only tested here; VL/Audio/Omni paths still untested on our side.

### sm120 NVFP4 check of the latest commits (head 8f6196da)

**Setup:** RTX 5060 8 GB (sm120), WSL2, torch 2.14.1+cu130, flashinfer 0.7.2, `LiquidAI/LFM3-1.7B-NVFP4` (W4A4, default `flashinfer_cutlass`), cookbook launch flags. A/B is 8f6196da vs its parent 917ed8fe.

**TL;DR:** 8f6196da is correct and a small win. Nothing in the new commits regresses NVFP4 prefill, decode, serving or GSM8K on sm120. Two small changes suggested below.

#### 8f6196da (conv launch bounded by the longest request)

- Bit-exact: across 300 random varlen batches (lengths at 1/255/256/257/512/1024, up to 128 requests, with initial state), outputs and final conv state are identical with `max_seq_len=max(lens)` and with the old total-token bound. A bound 256 tokens too small is caught in 225/225 cases, so the check can fail.
- Conv kernel time per prefill inside the model (torch profiler, 13 launches per forward):

| batch (requests x tokens) | conv before | conv after | whole forward (GPU) |
|---|---:|---:|---:|
| 1x2048 (control) | 1600 us | 1600 us | 71 ms |
| 64x32 | 1310 us | 1240 us | 68 ms |
| 128x16 | 1427 us | 1362 us | 69 ms |
| 16x1024 | 9213 us | 9106 us | 610 ms |
| 128x128 | 9845 us | 9224 us | 601 ms |

  That is at most ~0.1% of forward GPU time, so end-to-end prefill moves within noise.
- FYI: LFM3 never runs prefill under a CUDA graph. Both `sglang.benchmark.one_batch` and the server log `Disable prefill CUDA graph because some layers do not apply Standard GQA` (only `nemotron_h` sets `supports_hybrid_prefill_graph`), so every LFM3 prefill is eager and gets this bound.

#### Suggested changes

1. **Test the bound.** `Lfm3ShortConv.forward` now always passes `max_seq_len` (from `extend_seq_lens_cpu`), but `test_cutedsl_gated_conv.py` never does, so the kernel tests only cover the old bound. Suggest parametrizing `test_cute_prefill_across_chunk_boundary_with_initial_state` over `max_seq_len in (None, max(seqlens))` with a batch where the bound shrinks the grid, e.g. `seqlens = [600, 300, 3]` (4 chunks -> 3). With the current `[600, 3]` both bounds launch 3 chunks.
2. **Cookbook precision line is stale.** `docs/cookbook/autoregressive/LiquidAI/LFM3.mdx` says "BF16 (or FP16) checkpoints only — there is no packed-quantization (FP8/FP4) variant", but `LiquidAI/LFM3-1.7B-NVFP4` is public. On sm120 it serves with the generated command unchanged (`--trust-remote-code --reasoning-parser auto --tool-call-parser auto`; `modelopt_fp4` is auto-detected and the default FP4 GEMM is `flashinfer_cutlass`). Please update that line, and consider adding the NVFP4 variant to `lfm3.jsx` for the Blackwell targets you have verified. If that includes consumer cards, two things bit us on an 8 GB / 16 GB-RAM box:
   - With default flags the server captures decode CUDA graphs only for bs <= 8 (`bs=[1, 2, 4, 8]`), so 32 concurrent users drop to ~650 output tok/s; `--cuda-graph-max-bs-decode 64` brings it to ~2050 tok/s.
   - The first load JIT-builds FlashInfer's `fp4_gemm_cutlass_sm120` (17 CUTLASS objects); each `cicc` peaks ~4.2 GB, so the default parallel build is OOM-killed on a 16 GB host (ninja exit 137). Installing the prebuilt `flashinfer-jit-cache` (`flashinfer_jit_cache_sm120f`) or lowering `MAX_JOBS` avoids it.

<details><summary>NVFP4 bench at the PR head (8f6196da vs 917ed8fe differences are within run-to-run noise)</summary>

Single-request prefill (median of 20; the bound is a no-op for one request):

| prompt | latency | throughput |
|---|---:|---:|
| 512 | 29.4 ms | 17.4k tok/s |
| 2048 | 75.6 ms | 27.1k tok/s |
| 8192 | 307-335 ms | 24.5-26.6k tok/s |
| 16384 | 779 ms | 21.0k tok/s |

Decode (`one_batch`, median step over 127 steps; decode path unchanged by these commits):

| batch, context | step | throughput |
|---|---:|---:|
| 1, 256 | 6.0 ms | 166 tok/s |
| 1, 4096 | 6.2 ms | 162 tok/s |
| 8, 256 | 6.3 ms | 1.28k tok/s |
| 32, 256 | 7.2-7.5 ms | 4.3-4.5k tok/s |
| 64, 256 | 7.9-8.2 ms | 7.9-8.1k tok/s |

Serving (`sglang.benchmark.serving`, random token ids, cookbook launch):

| scenario | result |
|---|---:|
| 1 user, 512 in / 256 out | TPOT 5.24 ms, 186 output tok/s |
| 8 users, 1024 / 256 | 1.04-1.14k output tok/s |
| 32 users, 1024 / 256, default flags | 621-698 output tok/s (TPOT 32-38 ms) |
| 32 users, 1024 / 256, `--cuda-graph-max-bs-decode 64` | 2,052 output tok/s (TPOT 8.2 ms) |
| 64 users, same flag | 2,071 output tok/s (KV pool of ~32k tokens holds ~23 such requests) |
| 4 users, 4096 / 8 | 20.2-20.8k input tok/s |

GSM8K (sgl-eval, 200 examples, cookbook settings: temperature 1.0, top-p 0.95, seed 0): 95.5% (917ed8fe) / 95.0% (8f6196da), 100% stop rate.
</details>

<details><summary>Where GPU time goes on sm120 (profiler, PR head)</summary>

| phase | FP4 GEMM | FP4 act. quantize | BF16 GEMM/GEMV | attention | conv | rest |
|---|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|
| prefill 1x2048 | 24.4% | 3.4% | 51.1% | 5.8% | 2.2% | 13.1% |
| prefill 32x256 | 23.5% | 4.4% | 49.1% | 1.2% | 1.6% | 20.3% |
| decode bs=1, ctx 2048 | 32.9% | 1.0% | 59.7% (tied `lm_head` alone 25.2%) | 2.4% | 0.2% | 3.8% |
| decode bs=32, ctx 256 | 28.5% | 0.9% | 55.8% (tied `lm_head` alone 22.1%) | 9.2% | 0.8% | 4.7% |

The FP4 FFNs (1.13B params, 77% of the linear weights) run the block-scaled sm120 CUTLASS kernel at roughly 7x the effective throughput of the BF16 GEMMs, so the layers the checkpoint keeps in BF16 (`conv*` in/out proj, `self_attn*`, tied `lm_head`) take half or more of the GPU time. Not a PR issue; FYI for the quantization recipe.
</details>

**FYI on CI:** the red JIT kernel job is `test_gdn_prefill_graph.py`, which is broken on main since #46990 (`KVLayerRouter.from_layer_maps(pool, ())` raises `IndexError`). It runs here only because this PR touches `kernels/ops/mamba/`, and the `base-b` jobs fail fast behind it.

+"""Width-generic gated causal conv1d (CuTe DSL).
+
+Fuses a depthwise causal conv1d with its B/C gates: the input is packed
+`[B_gate | C_gate | x]`, so the kernel forms `Bx = B_gate * x`, runs the depthwise
+conv over the K-tap causal window, and multiplies the result by `C_gate` -- no
+transpose or permutation. Width-generic in K: the in-tree sgl_kernel C++
+causal_conv1d (widths 2-4) and the shared Triton kernel (widths 2-5) don't cover
+wider taps such as K=7 (e.g. LFM3's conv_L_cache=7), which this kernel serves. The
+conv is channel-parallel and memory-bound, so this is a SIMT kernel (no MMA/TMA): one
+thread owns one channel, and a warp's threads are adjacent channels, so each per-token
+read `proj[t, d..d+31]` is one coalesced transaction. Each thread keeps the K-1 causal
+window for its channel in registers (no shared memory, no barrier).
+
+Layout is token-major (T, dim) with `dim` contiguous -- sglang's native hidden-state
+layout, so no transpose is needed. Streamed tensors use the same descriptor idiom as
+the in-tree cutedsl_gdn / cutedsl_kda kernels:
+`from_dlpack(t.detach(), assumed_align=32).mark_layout_dynamic(leading_dim=...)`. The
+conv-state cache is left static so its slot offset folds to a compile-time stride and
+the int64 slot keeps the offset 64-bit (the cache can exceed 2**31 elements).
+
+Math is done in fp32 -- the operands are bf16/fp16, and fp32 accumulation matches the
+torch reference, whose `F.conv1d` / `.sum` reduce bf16 inputs in fp32 -- and the
+result is cast back to the tensor dtype.
+
+  decode : (B, dim) one token/req + (slots, dim, K-1) state -> (B, dim), state updated
+  prefill: (T, dim) varlen token-major + state + has_initial_state -> (T, dim)
+Validated against the PyTorch reference in tests/test_cutedsl_gated_conv.py.
+"""
+
+from __future__ import annotations
+
+import logging
+
+import cuda.bindings.driver as cuda
+import cutlass
+import cutlass.cute as cute
+import torch
+from cutlass.cute.runtime import from_dlpack
+
+logger = logging.getLogger(__name__)
+
+# Single compile cache for both ops, mirroring cutedsl_gdn / cutedsl_kda's
+# `_compiled_kernels`. `_compiled` is the one place that calls `cute.compile`.
+_compiled_kernels: dict = {}
+
+
+def _compiled(key, host_fn, *compile_args):
+    kernel = _compiled_kernels.get(key)
+    if kernel is None:
+        kernel = cute.compile(host_fn, *compile_args, options="--opt-level 3")
+        _compiled_kernels[key] = kernel
+        logger.info(f"CuTe DSL gated conv kernel compiled: {key}")
+    return kernel
+
+
+def _zero_bias(dim: int, device, dtype) -> torch.Tensor:
+    # Checkpoints with conv_bias=False (e.g. LFM3) give the wrappers bias=None; they
+    # pass this cached zero tensor (allocated once per (dim, device, dtype)) instead --
+    # the kernel keeps an unconditional `+ bias` so it stays branch-free, and a
+    # conv_bias=True checkpoint still works by passing a real bias.
+    key = (dim, str(device), dtype)
+    b = _zero_bias_cache.get(key)
+    if b is None:
+        b = torch.zeros(dim, device=device, dtype=dtype)
+        _zero_bias_cache[key] = b
+    return b
+
+
+_zero_bias_cache: dict = {}
+
+
+@cute.kernel
+def _decode_kernel(
+    mProj: cute.Tensor,  # (B, 3*dim)        packed in_proj output [B_gate | C_gate | x]
+    mW: cute.Tensor,  # (dim, K)          conv taps, static layout
+    mBias: cute.Tensor,  # (dim,)            conv bias (zeros when conv_bias=False)
+    mOut: cute.Tensor,  # (B, dim)          C_gate-gated conv output
+    mState: cute.Tensor,  # (slots, dim, K-1) rolling Bx window, static layout, mutated
+    mSlot: cute.Tensor,  # (B,) int64        per-request state-slot index
+    dim: cutlass.Int32,
+    SLOTS: cutlass.Constexpr,
+    K: cutlass.Constexpr,
+    BLOCK: cutlass.Constexpr,
+):
+    """One thread per channel for a one-token-per-request decode step.
+
+    For its (slot, channel) the thread loads the K-1 cached Bx values and the K conv
+    taps into fp32 registers, forms `Bx = B_gate * x` for the new token, computes the
+    depthwise dot (+bias), multiplies by `C_gate`, writes the output, and rolls the
+    state forward to `[old[1:], Bx]`. mProj columns are [0:dim)=B_gate, [dim:2dim)=C_gate,
+    [2dim:3dim)=x. Slots that are padded/out-of-range (<0 or >=SLOTS) are skipped.
+    """
+    tidx, _, _ = cute.arch.thread_idx()
+    bx, bb, _ = cute.arch.block_idx()
+    d = bx * BLOCK + tidx  # channel
+    cute.arch.griddepcontrol_wait()
+    slot = mSlot[bb]
+    if d < dim and slot >= 0 and slot < SLOTS:
+        mss = mState[slot, None, None]  # (dim, K-1) at the 64-bit slot offset
+        wv = cute.make_rmem_tensor(K, cutlass.Float32)
+        for k in cutlass.range_constexpr(K):
+            wv[k] = mW[d, k].to(cutlass.Float32)
+        win = cute.make_rmem_tensor(K - 1, cutlass.Float32)
+        for j in cutlass.range_constexpr(K - 1):
+            win[j] = mss[d, j].to(cutlass.Float32)
+        bxv = mProj[bb, d].to(cutlass.Float32) * mProj[bb, 2 * dim + d].to(
+            cutlass.Float32
+        )
+        cgate = mProj[bb, dim + d].to(cutlass.Float32)
+        acc = mBias[d].to(cutlass.Float32)
+        for j in cutlass.range_constexpr(K - 1):
+            acc = acc + win[j] * wv[j]
+        acc = acc + bxv * wv[K - 1]
+        mOut[bb, d] = (acc * cgate).to(mOut.element_type)
+        for j in cutlass.range_constexpr(K - 2):
+            mss[d, j] = win[j + 1].to(mState.element_type)
+        mss[d, K - 2] = bxv.to(mState.element_type)
+    cute.arch.griddepcontrol_launch_dependents()
+
+
+@cute.jit
+def _decode_host(
+    mProj,
+    mW,
+    mBias,
+    mOut,
+    mState,
+    mSlot,
+    dim: cutlass.Int32,
+    B: cutlass.Int32,
+    SLOTS: cutlass.Constexpr,
+    K: cutlass.Constexpr,
+    BLOCK: cutlass.Constexpr,
+    stream: cuda.CUstream,
+):
+    grid_d = (dim + BLOCK - 1) // BLOCK
+    _decode_kernel(mProj, mW, mBias, mOut, mState, mSlot, dim, SLOTS, K, BLOCK).launch(
+        grid=[grid_d, B, 1],
+        block=[BLOCK, 1, 1],
+        stream=stream,
+        use_pdl=True,
+    )
+
+
+def gated_causal_conv1d_decode(proj, conv_state, weight, bias, slot_idx, block=128):
+    """C-gated depthwise conv decode (one token per request).
+
+    Args:
+        proj: (B, 3*dim) packed in_proj output [B_gate | C_gate | x].
+        conv_state: (slots, dim, K-1) per-request rolling Bx window, mutated in place.
+        weight: (dim, K) conv taps.
+        bias: (dim,) conv bias, or None (conv_bias=False checkpoints).
+        slot_idx: (B,) state-slot index per request.
+        block: threads per block (channels per block).
+
+    Returns:
+        (B, dim) the C_gate-gated conv output. Bx=B_gate*x and the C_gate output gate
+        are fused into the kernel.
+    """
+    B = proj.shape[0]
+    dim = weight.shape[0]
+    K = weight.shape[-1]
+    slots = conv_state.shape[0]
+    out = proj.new_empty(B, dim)
+    bias_t = bias if bias is not None else _zero_bias(dim, proj.device, proj.dtype)
+    slot64 = slot_idx.detach().to(torch.int64)
+    mProj = from_dlpack(proj.detach(), assumed_align=32).mark_layout_dynamic(
+        leading_dim=1
+    )
+    mW = from_dlpack(weight.detach())
+    mB = from_dlpack(bias_t.detach(), assumed_align=32).mark_layout_dynamic(
+        leading_dim=0
+    )
+    mO = from_dlpack(out.detach(), assumed_align=32).mark_layout_dynamic(leading_dim=1)
+    mS = from_dlpack(conv_state.detach())
+    mSlot = from_dlpack(slot64, assumed_align=32).mark_layout_dynamic(leading_dim=0)
+    # Launch on torch's current stream (correct ordering + cuda-graph capture).
+    stream = cuda.CUstream(torch.cuda.current_stream().cuda_stream)
+    key = ("decode", dim, K, slots, block, proj.dtype, conv_state.dtype)
+    _compiled(
+        key, _decode_host, mProj, mW, mB, mO, mS, mSlot, dim, B, slots, K, block, stream
+    )(mProj, mW, mB, mO, mS, mSlot, dim, B, stream)
+    return out
+
+
+@cute.kernel
+def _prefill_kernel(
+    mProj: cute.Tensor,  # (T_total, 3*dim)  packed in_proj output [B_gate | C_gate | x]
+    mW: cute.Tensor,  # (dim, K)          conv taps
+    mBias: cute.Tensor,  # (dim,)            conv bias (zeros when conv_bias=False)
+    mOut: cute.Tensor,  # (T_total, dim)    C_gate-gated conv output
+    mState: cute.Tensor,  # (slots, dim, K-1) static, mutated
+    mQsl: cute.Tensor,  # (B+1,) int32      cumulative per-request token offsets
+    mSlot: cute.Tensor,  # (B,) int64        per-request state-slot index
+    mHasInit: cute.Tensor,  # (B,) int          1 if conv_state holds a real prefix
+    dim: cutlass.Int32,
+    SLOTS: cutlass.Constexpr,
+    K: cutlass.Constexpr,
+    CHUNK: cutlass.Constexpr,
+    BLOCK_D: cutlass.Constexpr,
+):
+    """One thread per channel, gridded over (d-tile, token-chunk, request) for varlen
+    prefill.
+
+    Each thread streams CHUNK tokens of one request for its channel, keeping the K-1
+    causal window of `Bx = B_gate * x` in registers; per-token reads coalesce across
+    the warp (dim contiguous). The window is seeded from conv_state when has_initial
+    (chunked prefill / carried prefix) else zero, and the chunk holding the request's
+    last token writes the final window back as the new state. mProj columns are
+    [0:dim)=B_gate, [dim:2dim)=C_gate, [2dim:3dim)=x. Out-of-range slots are skipped.
+    """
+    tidx, _, _ = cute.arch.thread_idx()  # channel within the d-tile
+    bdx, bc, bb = cute.arch.block_idx()  # d-tile, token-chunk, request
+    d = bdx * BLOCK_D + tidx
+    cute.arch.griddepcontrol_wait()
+    s = mQsl[bb]
+    e = mQsl[bb + 1]
+    treq = e - s
+    c0 = bc * CHUNK  # first token of this chunk within the request
+    slot = mSlot[bb]
+    if d < dim and c0 < treq and slot >= 0 and slot < SLOTS:
+        mss = mState[slot, None, None]  # (dim, K-1) at int64 slot offset
+        has_init = mHasInit[bb]
+        wv = cute.make_rmem_tensor(K, cutlass.Float32)
+        for k in cutlass.range_constexpr(K):
+            wv[k] = mW[d, k].to(cutlass.Float32)
+        bias = mBias[d].to(cutlass.Float32)
+        win = cute.make_rmem_tensor(K - 1, cutlass.Float32)
+        for j in cutlass.range_constexpr(K - 1):
+            r = c0 - (K - 1) + j  # req-token index for window slot j (oldest first)
+            hv = cutlass.Float32(0.0)
+            if r >= 0:
+                hv = mProj[s + r, d].to(cutlass.Float32) * mProj[s + r, 2 * dim + d].to(
+                    cutlass.Float32
+                )  # B_gate*x
+            elif has_init != 0:
+                hv = mss[d, (K - 1) + r].to(
+                    cutlass.Float32
+                )  # before request -> initial state
+            win[j] = hv
+        cend = c0 + CHUNK
+        if cend > treq:
+            cend = treq
+        t = c0
+        while t < cend:
+            bxv = mProj[s + t, d].to(cutlass.Float32) * mProj[s + t, 2 * dim + d].to(
+                cutlass.Float32
+            )  # B_gate*x
+            cgate = mProj[s + t, dim + d].to(cutlass.Float32)
+            acc = bias
+            for j in cutlass.range_constexpr(K - 1):
+                acc = acc + win[j] * wv[j]
+            acc = acc + bxv * wv[K - 1]
+            mOut[s + t, d] = (acc * cgate).to(mOut.element_type)
+            for j in cutlass.range_constexpr(K - 2):
+                win[j] = win[j + 1]
+            win[K - 2] = bxv
+            t = t + 1
+        if cend == treq:
+            for j in cutlass.range_constexpr(K - 1):
+                mss[d, j] = win[j].to(mState.element_type)

+"""
+LFM3 (Liquid Foundation Model 3) implementation for SGLang.
+
+Hybrid architecture with three layer flavors:
+  - `full_attention`: GQA with partial-RoPE (global rope_theta, e.g. 1e6)
+  - `sliding_attention`: GQA with full-RoPE (SWA rope_theta, e.g. 1e4)
+                        + RadixAttention sliding_window_size
+  - `conv`: gated short-conv (B*x -> CuTe DSL causal-conv1d -> C*conv_out)
+
+Adds over LFM2:
+  - Per-layer SWA via `RadixAttention(sliding_window_size=...)`
+  - Two RoPE tables (global partial-RoPE + local full-RoPE) routed by layer_type
+  - Per-head sigmoid gate on the attention output (`gate_proj`, always on)
+  - Optional sandwich norm (`use_sandwich_norm`): extra RMSNorm AFTER the
+    operator and AFTER the FFN
+
+Attention layers use RadixAttention; conv layers use the MambaPool conv-state
+cache (via HybridReqToTokenPool) with a width-generic CuTe DSL causal-conv1d
+kernel (`sglang.kernels.ops.mamba.cutedsl_gated_conv`) for both prefill and decode.
+"""

+from collections.abc import Iterable

+@torch.compile(dynamic=True, backend=get_compiler_backend())
+def _lfm3_apply_headwise_gate(
+    gate_logits: torch.Tensor,
+    attn_out: torch.Tensor,
+    T: int,
+    num_heads: int,
+    head_dim: int,
+) -> torch.Tensor:
+    """Inductor-fused sigmoid + view + mul + reshape for headwise gated attention.
+
+    Same shape as llama4's `_mul_attn_scale` and Qwen3-Next's
+    `_apply_q_scale_and_softmax_scale` -- a tiny pure-math elementwise function
+    that benefits from being compiled into a single kernel under
+    `dynamic=True`.
+    """
+    gate = torch.sigmoid(gate_logits).view(T, num_heads, 1)
+    return (gate * attn_out.view(T, num_heads, head_dim)).reshape(T, -1)
+
+
+@torch.compile(dynamic=True, backend=get_compiler_backend())
+def _lfm3_conv_input_gate(
+    proj: torch.Tensor,
+) -> tuple[torch.Tensor, torch.Tensor]:
+    """Split packed in_proj [B_gate | C_gate | x] and form the conv input Bx=B_gate*x.
+
+    Returns (Bx, C_gate) for the torch fallback. The CuTe kernel fuses
+    this split and both gates internally.
+    """
+    B_gate, C_gate, x = proj.chunk(3, dim=-1)
+    return B_gate * x, C_gate
+
+
+@torch.compile(dynamic=True, backend=get_compiler_backend())
+def _lfm3_conv_decode_torch(
+    proj: torch.Tensor,
+    conv_state: torch.Tensor,
+    weight: torch.Tensor,
+    bias: torch.Tensor | None,
+    mamba_indices: torch.Tensor,
+) -> torch.Tensor:
+    """Compiled gated convolution update when the CuTe kernel is unavailable.
+
+    Form B*x, convolve its rolling K-token window, apply C, and advance
+    the per-request state in place.
+    """
+    B_gate, C_gate, x = proj.chunk(3, dim=-1)
+    Bx = B_gate * x
+    sel = conv_state[mamba_indices].to(Bx.dtype)
+    window = torch.cat([sel, Bx.unsqueeze(-1)], dim=-1)
+    w = weight.to(Bx.dtype)
+    out = (window * w.unsqueeze(0)).sum(dim=-1)
+    if bias is not None:
+        out = out + bias.to(out.dtype)
+    conv_state[mamba_indices] = window[:, :, 1:].to(conv_state.dtype)
+    return C_gate * out
+

+# kernel module's `_zero_bias` caching.
+_ONES_FLAGS_CACHE: dict = {}

+        prefix: str = "",

+            [config.intermediate_size, config.intermediate_size],

+            quant_config=quant_config,
+            prefix=add_prefix("gate_up_proj", prefix),

+            config.hidden_size,

+
+    For partial RoPE, use rope_type="proportional" (SGLang's Gemma4RotaryEmbedding),
+    which matches HF LFM3's Gemma-4-style rotation pairing; the plain RotaryEmbedding

+    # so index it directly -- a default here would silently inject a wrong theta.
+    base = rope_parameters["rope_theta"]
+    rope_type = rope_parameters.get("rope_type", "default")

+    overrides); they differ only in the RoPE table and the window.
+    """

+    def __init__(

+        sliding_window: int | None = None,

+        prefix: str = "",
+        alt_stream: torch.cuda.Stream | None = None,

+        layer_key = (

+            quant_config=quant_config,
+            prefix=add_prefix("qkv_proj", prefix),

+            self.hidden_size,
+            bias=False,

+            head_dim=self.head_dim,
+            scaling=self.scaling,
+            num_kv_heads=self.num_local_kv_heads,
+            layer_id=layer_id,

+            # DISTANCE, so pass sliding_window - 1 (matches gemma2 / exaone4 / afmoe and

+            # layers would attend to one extra token vs HF.
+            sliding_window_size=(

+            prefix=add_prefix("attn", prefix),

+    def forward(
+        self,

+        # on alt_stream under cuda-graph capture below a token threshold; above

+        # overlaps them, so the manual path is off then. Same gate as

Paged prefill is a correctness requirement for this model, not a tunable default: fail loudly on an explicit false, or set it unconditionally.

+`Lfm3ShortConv._conv_prefill` / `_conv_decode` (which match HF `slow_forward`), and the
+kernel is checked against that reference for prefill (varlen, with/without initial
+state) and decode.
+
+Run:
+    python -m pytest test/registered/kernels/ops/mamba/test_cutedsl_gated_conv.py -v

+

+
+import pytest
+import torch
+import torch.nn.functional as F
+
+from sglang.test.ci.ci_register import register_cuda_ci
+
+register_cuda_ci(est_time=30, stage="base-b-kernel-unit", runner_config="1-gpu-large")
+
+
+# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
+# Reference semantics (the contract the CuTe kernel must satisfy)
+# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
+def ref_conv_decode(
+    Bx: torch.Tensor,  # (B, dim) one new token per request
+    conv_state: torch.Tensor,  # (num_slots, dim, K-1) holds last K-1 inputs, mutated
+    weight: torch.Tensor,  # (dim, K)
+    bias: torch.Tensor | None,  # (dim,) or None
+    slot_idx: torch.Tensor,  # (B,) int32 -> row in conv_state
+) -> torch.Tensor:
+    """Single-token rolling update. Mirrors Lfm3ShortConv._conv_decode."""
+    K = weight.shape[-1]
+    sel = conv_state[slot_idx].to(Bx.dtype)  # (B, dim, K-1)
+    window = torch.cat([sel, Bx.unsqueeze(-1)], dim=-1)  # (B, dim, K)
+    out = (window * weight.to(Bx.dtype).unsqueeze(0)).sum(-1)  # (B, dim)
+    if bias is not None:
+        out = out + bias.to(out.dtype)
+    conv_state[slot_idx] = window[:, :, 1:].to(conv_state.dtype)
+    return out
+
+
+def ref_conv_prefill(
+    Bx_t: torch.Tensor,  # (dim, total_tokens) channel-major, varlen-concat
+    conv_state: torch.Tensor,  # (num_slots, dim, K-1), mutated
+    weight: torch.Tensor,  # (dim, K)
+    bias: torch.Tensor | None,  # (dim,) or None
+    query_start_loc: torch.Tensor,  # (B+1,) int32 cumulative token offsets
+    slot_idx: torch.Tensor,  # (B,) int32
+    has_initial_state: torch.Tensor,  # (B,) bool
+) -> torch.Tensor:
+    """Per-request causal depthwise conv. Mirrors Lfm3ShortConv._conv_prefill +
+    the has_initial_state handling from Lfm2ShortConv (chunked-prefill safe)."""
+    dim, K = weight.shape
+    w = weight.to(Bx_t.dtype).unsqueeze(1)  # (dim,1,K)
+    b = bias.to(Bx_t.dtype) if bias is not None else None
+    starts = query_start_loc.tolist()
+    slots = slot_idx.tolist()
+    init = has_initial_state.tolist()
+    out_chunks = []
+    for i, slot in enumerate(slots):
+        s, e = starts[i], starts[i + 1]
+        if s == e:
+            continue
+        seg = Bx_t[:, s:e]  # (dim, T_i)
+        if init[i]:
+            state_i = conv_state[slot].to(Bx_t.dtype)  # (dim, K-1)
+        else:
+            state_i = torch.zeros(dim, K - 1, device=Bx_t.device, dtype=Bx_t.dtype)

+# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
+# Kernel-under-test hook (CuTe DSL kernel plugs in here once written)
+# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
+def _load_cute_kernel():
+    try:
+        from sglang.kernels.ops.mamba.cutedsl_gated_conv import (  # noqa: F401
+            gated_causal_conv1d_decode,
+            gated_causal_conv1d_prefill,
+        )

+        return gated_causal_conv1d_prefill, gated_causal_conv1d_decode
+    except Exception:

+# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------

+# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------

+"""Width-generic gated causal conv1d (CuTe DSL).
+
+Fuses a depthwise causal conv1d with its B/C gates: the input is packed
+`[B_gate | C_gate | x]`, so the kernel forms `Bx = B_gate * x`, runs the depthwise
+conv over the K-tap causal window, and multiplies the result by `C_gate` -- no
+transpose or permutation. Width-generic in K: the in-tree sgl_kernel C++
+causal_conv1d (widths 2-4) and the shared Triton kernel (widths 2-5) don't cover
+wider taps such as K=7 (e.g. LFM3's conv_L_cache=7), which this kernel serves. The
+conv is channel-parallel and memory-bound, so this is a SIMT kernel (no MMA/TMA): one
+thread owns one channel, and a warp's threads are adjacent channels, so each per-token
+read `proj[t, d..d+31]` is one coalesced transaction. Each thread keeps the K-1 causal
+window for its channel in registers (no shared memory, no barrier).
+
+Layout is token-major (T, dim) with `dim` contiguous -- sglang's native hidden-state
+layout, so no transpose is needed. Streamed tensors use the same descriptor idiom as
+the in-tree cutedsl_gdn / cutedsl_kda kernels:
+`from_dlpack(t.detach(), assumed_align=32).mark_layout_dynamic(leading_dim=...)`. The
+conv-state cache is left static so its slot offset folds to a compile-time stride and
+the int64 slot keeps the offset 64-bit (the cache can exceed 2**31 elements).
+
+Math is done in fp32 -- the operands are bf16/fp16, and fp32 accumulation matches the
+torch reference, whose `F.conv1d` / `.sum` reduce bf16 inputs in fp32 -- and the
+result is cast back to the tensor dtype.
+
+  decode : (B, dim) one token/req + (slots, dim, K-1) state -> (B, dim), state updated
+  prefill: (T, dim) varlen token-major + state + has_initial_state -> (T, dim)
+Validated against the PyTorch reference in tests/test_cutedsl_gated_conv.py.
+"""
+
+from __future__ import annotations
+
+import logging
+
+import cuda.bindings.driver as cuda
+import cutlass
+import cutlass.cute as cute
+import torch
+from cutlass.cute.runtime import from_dlpack
+
+logger = logging.getLogger(__name__)
+
+# Single compile cache for both ops, mirroring cutedsl_gdn / cutedsl_kda's
+# `_compiled_kernels`. `_compiled` is the one place that calls `cute.compile`.
+_compiled_kernels: dict = {}
+
+
+def _compiled(key, host_fn, *compile_args):
+    kernel = _compiled_kernels.get(key)
+    if kernel is None:
+        kernel = cute.compile(host_fn, *compile_args, options="--opt-level 3")
+        _compiled_kernels[key] = kernel
+        logger.info(f"CuTe DSL gated conv kernel compiled: {key}")
+    return kernel
+
+
+def _zero_bias(dim: int, device, dtype) -> torch.Tensor:
+    # Checkpoints with conv_bias=False (e.g. LFM3) give the wrappers bias=None; they
+    # pass this cached zero tensor (allocated once per (dim, device, dtype)) instead --
+    # the kernel keeps an unconditional `+ bias` so it stays branch-free, and a
+    # conv_bias=True checkpoint still works by passing a real bias.
+    key = (dim, str(device), dtype)
+    b = _zero_bias_cache.get(key)
+    if b is None:
+        b = torch.zeros(dim, device=device, dtype=dtype)
+        _zero_bias_cache[key] = b
+    return b
+
+
+_zero_bias_cache: dict = {}
+
+
+@cute.kernel
+def _decode_kernel(
+    mProj: cute.Tensor,  # (B, 3*dim)        packed in_proj output [B_gate | C_gate | x]
+    mW: cute.Tensor,  # (dim, K)          conv taps, static layout
+    mBias: cute.Tensor,  # (dim,)            conv bias (zeros when conv_bias=False)
+    mOut: cute.Tensor,  # (B, dim)          C_gate-gated conv output
+    mState: cute.Tensor,  # (slots, dim, K-1) rolling Bx window, static layout, mutated
+    mSlot: cute.Tensor,  # (B,) int64        per-request state-slot index
+    dim: cutlass.Int32,
+    SLOTS: cutlass.Constexpr,
+    K: cutlass.Constexpr,
+    BLOCK: cutlass.Constexpr,
+):
+    """One thread per channel for a one-token-per-request decode step.
+
+    For its (slot, channel) the thread loads the K-1 cached Bx values and the K conv
+    taps into fp32 registers, forms `Bx = B_gate * x` for the new token, computes the
+    depthwise dot (+bias), multiplies by `C_gate`, writes the output, and rolls the
+    state forward to `[old[1:], Bx]`. mProj columns are [0:dim)=B_gate, [dim:2dim)=C_gate,
+    [2dim:3dim)=x. Slots that are padded/out-of-range (<0 or >=SLOTS) are skipped.
+    """
+    tidx, _, _ = cute.arch.thread_idx()
+    bx, bb, _ = cute.arch.block_idx()
+    d = bx * BLOCK + tidx  # channel
+    cute.arch.griddepcontrol_wait()
+    slot = mSlot[bb]
+    if d < dim and slot >= 0 and slot < SLOTS:
+        mss = mState[slot, None, None]  # (dim, K-1) at the 64-bit slot offset
+        wv = cute.make_rmem_tensor(K, cutlass.Float32)
+        for k in cutlass.range_constexpr(K):
+            wv[k] = mW[d, k].to(cutlass.Float32)
+        win = cute.make_rmem_tensor(K - 1, cutlass.Float32)
+        for j in cutlass.range_constexpr(K - 1):
+            win[j] = mss[d, j].to(cutlass.Float32)
+        bxv = mProj[bb, d].to(cutlass.Float32) * mProj[bb, 2 * dim + d].to(
+            cutlass.Float32
+        )
+        cgate = mProj[bb, dim + d].to(cutlass.Float32)
+        acc = mBias[d].to(cutlass.Float32)
+        for j in cutlass.range_constexpr(K - 1):
+            acc = acc + win[j] * wv[j]
+        acc = acc + bxv * wv[K - 1]
+        mOut[bb, d] = (acc * cgate).to(mOut.element_type)
+        for j in cutlass.range_constexpr(K - 2):
+            mss[d, j] = win[j + 1].to(mState.element_type)
+        mss[d, K - 2] = bxv.to(mState.element_type)
+    cute.arch.griddepcontrol_launch_dependents()
+
+
+@cute.jit
+def _decode_host(
+    mProj,
+    mW,
+    mBias,
+    mOut,
+    mState,
+    mSlot,
+    dim: cutlass.Int32,
+    B: cutlass.Int32,
+    SLOTS: cutlass.Constexpr,
+    K: cutlass.Constexpr,
+    BLOCK: cutlass.Constexpr,
+    stream: cuda.CUstream,
+):
+    grid_d = (dim + BLOCK - 1) // BLOCK
+    _decode_kernel(mProj, mW, mBias, mOut, mState, mSlot, dim, SLOTS, K, BLOCK).launch(
+        grid=[grid_d, B, 1],
+        block=[BLOCK, 1, 1],
+        stream=stream,
+        use_pdl=True,
+    )
+
+
+def gated_causal_conv1d_decode(proj, conv_state, weight, bias, slot_idx, block=128):
+    """C-gated depthwise conv decode (one token per request).
+
+    Args:
+        proj: (B, 3*dim) packed in_proj output [B_gate | C_gate | x].
+        conv_state: (slots, dim, K-1) per-request rolling Bx window, mutated in place.
+        weight: (dim, K) conv taps.
+        bias: (dim,) conv bias, or None (conv_bias=False checkpoints).
+        slot_idx: (B,) state-slot index per request.
+        block: threads per block (channels per block).
+
+    Returns:
+        (B, dim) the C_gate-gated conv output. Bx=B_gate*x and the C_gate output gate
+        are fused into the kernel.
+    """
+    B = proj.shape[0]
+    dim = weight.shape[0]
+    K = weight.shape[-1]
+    slots = conv_state.shape[0]
+    out = proj.new_empty(B, dim)
+    bias_t = bias if bias is not None else _zero_bias(dim, proj.device, proj.dtype)
+    slot64 = slot_idx.detach().to(torch.int64)
+    mProj = from_dlpack(proj.detach(), assumed_align=32).mark_layout_dynamic(
+        leading_dim=1
+    )
+    mW = from_dlpack(weight.detach())
+    mB = from_dlpack(bias_t.detach(), assumed_align=32).mark_layout_dynamic(
+        leading_dim=0
+    )
+    mO = from_dlpack(out.detach(), assumed_align=32).mark_layout_dynamic(leading_dim=1)
+    mS = from_dlpack(conv_state.detach())
+    mSlot = from_dlpack(slot64, assumed_align=32).mark_layout_dynamic(leading_dim=0)
+    # Launch on torch's current stream (correct ordering + cuda-graph capture).
+    stream = cuda.CUstream(torch.cuda.current_stream().cuda_stream)
+    key = ("decode", dim, K, slots, block, proj.dtype, conv_state.dtype)
+    _compiled(
+        key, _decode_host, mProj, mW, mB, mO, mS, mSlot, dim, B, slots, K, block, stream
+    )(mProj, mW, mB, mO, mS, mSlot, dim, B, stream)
+    return out
+
+
+@cute.kernel
+def _prefill_kernel(
+    mProj: cute.Tensor,  # (T_total, 3*dim)  packed in_proj output [B_gate | C_gate | x]
+    mW: cute.Tensor,  # (dim, K)          conv taps
+    mBias: cute.Tensor,  # (dim,)            conv bias (zeros when conv_bias=False)
+    mOut: cute.Tensor,  # (T_total, dim)    C_gate-gated conv output
+    mState: cute.Tensor,  # (slots, dim, K-1) static, mutated
+    mQsl: cute.Tensor,  # (B+1,) int32      cumulative per-request token offsets
+    mSlot: cute.Tensor,  # (B,) int64        per-request state-slot index
+    mHasInit: cute.Tensor,  # (B,) int          1 if conv_state holds a real prefix
+    dim: cutlass.Int32,
+    SLOTS: cutlass.Constexpr,
+    K: cutlass.Constexpr,
+    CHUNK: cutlass.Constexpr,
+    BLOCK_D: cutlass.Constexpr,
+):
+    """One thread per channel, gridded over (d-tile, token-chunk, request) for varlen
+    prefill.
+
+    Each thread streams CHUNK tokens of one request for its channel, keeping the K-1
+    causal window of `Bx = B_gate * x` in registers; per-token reads coalesce across
+    the warp (dim contiguous). The window is seeded from conv_state when has_initial
+    (chunked prefill / carried prefix) else zero, and the chunk holding the request's
+    last token writes the final window back as the new state. mProj columns are
+    [0:dim)=B_gate, [dim:2dim)=C_gate, [2dim:3dim)=x. Out-of-range slots are skipped.
+    """
+    tidx, _, _ = cute.arch.thread_idx()  # channel within the d-tile
+    bdx, bc, bb = cute.arch.block_idx()  # d-tile, token-chunk, request
+    d = bdx * BLOCK_D + tidx
+    cute.arch.griddepcontrol_wait()
+    s = mQsl[bb]
+    e = mQsl[bb + 1]
+    treq = e - s
+    c0 = bc * CHUNK  # first token of this chunk within the request
+    slot = mSlot[bb]
+    if d < dim and c0 < treq and slot >= 0 and slot < SLOTS:
+        mss = mState[slot, None, None]  # (dim, K-1) at int64 slot offset
+        has_init = mHasInit[bb]
+        wv = cute.make_rmem_tensor(K, cutlass.Float32)
+        for k in cutlass.range_constexpr(K):
+            wv[k] = mW[d, k].to(cutlass.Float32)
+        bias = mBias[d].to(cutlass.Float32)
+        win = cute.make_rmem_tensor(K - 1, cutlass.Float32)
+        for j in cutlass.range_constexpr(K - 1):
+            r = c0 - (K - 1) + j  # req-token index for window slot j (oldest first)
+            hv = cutlass.Float32(0.0)
+            if r >= 0:
+                hv = mProj[s + r, d].to(cutlass.Float32) * mProj[s + r, 2 * dim + d].to(
+                    cutlass.Float32
+                )  # B_gate*x
+            elif has_init != 0:
+                hv = mss[d, (K - 1) + r].to(
+                    cutlass.Float32
+                )  # before request -> initial state
+            win[j] = hv
+        cend = c0 + CHUNK
+        if cend > treq:
+            cend = treq
+        t = c0
+        while t < cend:
+            bxv = mProj[s + t, d].to(cutlass.Float32) * mProj[s + t, 2 * dim + d].to(
+                cutlass.Float32
+            )  # B_gate*x
+            cgate = mProj[s + t, dim + d].to(cutlass.Float32)
+            acc = bias
+            for j in cutlass.range_constexpr(K - 1):
+                acc = acc + win[j] * wv[j]
+            acc = acc + bxv * wv[K - 1]
+            mOut[s + t, d] = (acc * cgate).to(mOut.element_type)
+            for j in cutlass.range_constexpr(K - 2):
+                win[j] = win[j + 1]
+            win[K - 2] = bxv
+            t = t + 1
+        if cend == treq:
+            for j in cutlass.range_constexpr(K - 1):
+                mss[d, j] = win[j].to(mState.element_type)
+    cute.arch.griddepcontrol_launch_dependents()
+
+
+@cute.jit
+def _prefill_host(
+    mProj,
+    mW,
+    mBias,
+    mOut,
+    mState,
+    mQsl,
+    mSlot,
+    mHasInit,
+    dim: cutlass.Int32,
+    n_chunks: cutlass.Int32,
+    B: cutlass.Int32,
+    SLOTS: cutlass.Constexpr,
+    K: cutlass.Constexpr,
+    CHUNK: cutlass.Constexpr,
+    BLOCK_D: cutlass.Constexpr,
+    stream: cuda.CUstream,
+):
+    grid_d = (dim + BLOCK_D - 1) // BLOCK_D
+    _prefill_kernel(
+        mProj,
+        mW,
+        mBias,
+        mOut,
+        mState,
+        mQsl,
+        mSlot,
+        mHasInit,
+        dim,
+        SLOTS,
+        K,
+        CHUNK,
+        BLOCK_D,
+    ).launch(
+        grid=[grid_d, n_chunks, B], block=[BLOCK_D, 1, 1], stream=stream, use_pdl=True

+"""Width-generic gated causal conv1d (CuTe DSL).
+
+Fuses a depthwise causal conv1d with its B/C gates: the input is packed
+`[B_gate | C_gate | x]`, so the kernel forms `Bx = B_gate * x`, runs the depthwise
+conv over the K-tap causal window, and multiplies the result by `C_gate` -- no
+transpose or permutation. Width-generic in K: the in-tree sgl_kernel C++
+causal_conv1d (widths 2-4) and the shared Triton kernel (widths 2-5) don't cover
+wider taps such as K=7 (e.g. LFM3's conv_L_cache=7), which this kernel serves. The
+conv is channel-parallel and memory-bound, so this is a SIMT kernel (no MMA/TMA): one
+thread owns one channel, and a warp's threads are adjacent channels, so each per-token
+read `proj[t, d..d+31]` is one coalesced transaction. Each thread keeps the K-1 causal
+window for its channel in registers (no shared memory, no barrier).
+
+Layout is token-major (T, dim) with `dim` contiguous -- sglang's native hidden-state
+layout, so no transpose is needed. Streamed tensors use the same descriptor idiom as
+the in-tree cutedsl_gdn / cutedsl_kda kernels:
+`from_dlpack(t.detach(), assumed_align=32).mark_layout_dynamic(leading_dim=...)`. The
+conv-state cache is left static so its slot offset folds to a compile-time stride and
+the int64 slot keeps the offset 64-bit (the cache can exceed 2**31 elements).
+
+Math is done in fp32 -- the operands are bf16/fp16, and fp32 accumulation matches the
+torch reference, whose `F.conv1d` / `.sum` reduce bf16 inputs in fp32 -- and the
+result is cast back to the tensor dtype.
+
+  decode : (B, dim) one token/req + (slots, dim, K-1) state -> (B, dim), state updated
+  prefill: (T, dim) varlen token-major + state + has_initial_state -> (T, dim)
+Validated against the PyTorch reference in tests/test_cutedsl_gated_conv.py.
+"""
+
+from __future__ import annotations
+
+import logging
+
+import cuda.bindings.driver as cuda
+import cutlass
+import cutlass.cute as cute
+import torch
+from cutlass.cute.runtime import from_dlpack
+
+logger = logging.getLogger(__name__)
+
+# Single compile cache for both ops, mirroring cutedsl_gdn / cutedsl_kda's
+# `_compiled_kernels`. `_compiled` is the one place that calls `cute.compile`.
+_compiled_kernels: dict = {}
+
+
+def _compiled(key, host_fn, *compile_args):
+    kernel = _compiled_kernels.get(key)
+    if kernel is None:
+        kernel = cute.compile(host_fn, *compile_args, options="--opt-level 3")
+        _compiled_kernels[key] = kernel
+        logger.info(f"CuTe DSL gated conv kernel compiled: {key}")
+    return kernel
+
+
+def _zero_bias(dim: int, device, dtype) -> torch.Tensor:
+    # Checkpoints with conv_bias=False (e.g. LFM3) give the wrappers bias=None; they
+    # pass this cached zero tensor (allocated once per (dim, device, dtype)) instead --
+    # the kernel keeps an unconditional `+ bias` so it stays branch-free, and a
+    # conv_bias=True checkpoint still works by passing a real bias.
+    key = (dim, str(device), dtype)
+    b = _zero_bias_cache.get(key)
+    if b is None:
+        b = torch.zeros(dim, device=device, dtype=dtype)
+        _zero_bias_cache[key] = b
+    return b
+
+
+_zero_bias_cache: dict = {}
+
+
+@cute.kernel
+def _decode_kernel(
+    mProj: cute.Tensor,  # (B, 3*dim)        packed in_proj output [B_gate | C_gate | x]
+    mW: cute.Tensor,  # (dim, K)          conv taps, static layout
+    mBias: cute.Tensor,  # (dim,)            conv bias (zeros when conv_bias=False)
+    mOut: cute.Tensor,  # (B, dim)          C_gate-gated conv output
+    mState: cute.Tensor,  # (slots, dim, K-1) rolling Bx window, static layout, mutated
+    mSlot: cute.Tensor,  # (B,) int64        per-request state-slot index
+    dim: cutlass.Int32,
+    SLOTS: cutlass.Constexpr,
+    K: cutlass.Constexpr,
+    BLOCK: cutlass.Constexpr,
+):
+    """One thread per channel for a one-token-per-request decode step.
+
+    For its (slot, channel) the thread loads the K-1 cached Bx values and the K conv
+    taps into fp32 registers, forms `Bx = B_gate * x` for the new token, computes the
+    depthwise dot (+bias), multiplies by `C_gate`, writes the output, and rolls the
+    state forward to `[old[1:], Bx]`. mProj columns are [0:dim)=B_gate, [dim:2dim)=C_gate,
+    [2dim:3dim)=x. Slots that are padded/out-of-range (<0 or >=SLOTS) are skipped.
+    """
+    tidx, _, _ = cute.arch.thread_idx()
+    bx, bb, _ = cute.arch.block_idx()
+    d = bx * BLOCK + tidx  # channel
+    cute.arch.griddepcontrol_wait()
+    slot = mSlot[bb]
+    if d < dim and slot >= 0 and slot < SLOTS:
+        mss = mState[slot, None, None]  # (dim, K-1) at the 64-bit slot offset
+        wv = cute.make_rmem_tensor(K, cutlass.Float32)
+        for k in cutlass.range_constexpr(K):
+            wv[k] = mW[d, k].to(cutlass.Float32)
+        win = cute.make_rmem_tensor(K - 1, cutlass.Float32)
+        for j in cutlass.range_constexpr(K - 1):
+            win[j] = mss[d, j].to(cutlass.Float32)
+        bxv = mProj[bb, d].to(cutlass.Float32) * mProj[bb, 2 * dim + d].to(
+            cutlass.Float32
+        )
+        cgate = mProj[bb, dim + d].to(cutlass.Float32)
+        acc = mBias[d].to(cutlass.Float32)
+        for j in cutlass.range_constexpr(K - 1):
+            acc = acc + win[j] * wv[j]
+        acc = acc + bxv * wv[K - 1]
+        mOut[bb, d] = (acc * cgate).to(mOut.element_type)
+        for j in cutlass.range_constexpr(K - 2):
+            mss[d, j] = win[j + 1].to(mState.element_type)
+        mss[d, K - 2] = bxv.to(mState.element_type)
+    cute.arch.griddepcontrol_launch_dependents()
+
+
+@cute.jit
+def _decode_host(
+    mProj,
+    mW,
+    mBias,
+    mOut,
+    mState,
+    mSlot,
+    dim: cutlass.Int32,
+    B: cutlass.Int32,
+    SLOTS: cutlass.Constexpr,
+    K: cutlass.Constexpr,
+    BLOCK: cutlass.Constexpr,
+    stream: cuda.CUstream,
+):
+    grid_d = (dim + BLOCK - 1) // BLOCK
+    _decode_kernel(mProj, mW, mBias, mOut, mState, mSlot, dim, SLOTS, K, BLOCK).launch(
+        grid=[grid_d, B, 1],
+        block=[BLOCK, 1, 1],
+        stream=stream,
+        use_pdl=True,
+    )
+
+
+def gated_causal_conv1d_decode(proj, conv_state, weight, bias, slot_idx, block=128):
+    """C-gated depthwise conv decode (one token per request).
+
+    Args:
+        proj: (B, 3*dim) packed in_proj output [B_gate | C_gate | x].
+        conv_state: (slots, dim, K-1) per-request rolling Bx window, mutated in place.
+        weight: (dim, K) conv taps.
+        bias: (dim,) conv bias, or None (conv_bias=False checkpoints).
+        slot_idx: (B,) state-slot index per request.
+        block: threads per block (channels per block).
+
+    Returns:
+        (B, dim) the C_gate-gated conv output. Bx=B_gate*x and the C_gate output gate
+        are fused into the kernel.
+    """
+    B = proj.shape[0]
+    dim = weight.shape[0]
+    K = weight.shape[-1]
+    slots = conv_state.shape[0]
+    out = proj.new_empty(B, dim)
+    bias_t = bias if bias is not None else _zero_bias(dim, proj.device, proj.dtype)
+    slot64 = slot_idx.detach().to(torch.int64)
+    mProj = from_dlpack(proj.detach(), assumed_align=32).mark_layout_dynamic(
+        leading_dim=1
+    )
+    mW = from_dlpack(weight.detach())
+    mB = from_dlpack(bias_t.detach(), assumed_align=32).mark_layout_dynamic(
+        leading_dim=0
+    )
+    mO = from_dlpack(out.detach(), assumed_align=32).mark_layout_dynamic(leading_dim=1)
+    mS = from_dlpack(conv_state.detach())
+    mSlot = from_dlpack(slot64, assumed_align=32).mark_layout_dynamic(leading_dim=0)
+    # Launch on torch's current stream (correct ordering + cuda-graph capture).
+    stream = cuda.CUstream(torch.cuda.current_stream().cuda_stream)
+    key = ("decode", dim, K, slots, block, proj.dtype, conv_state.dtype)
+    _compiled(
+        key, _decode_host, mProj, mW, mB, mO, mS, mSlot, dim, B, slots, K, block, stream
+    )(mProj, mW, mB, mO, mS, mSlot, dim, B, stream)
+    return out
+
+
+@cute.kernel
+def _prefill_kernel(
+    mProj: cute.Tensor,  # (T_total, 3*dim)  packed in_proj output [B_gate | C_gate | x]
+    mW: cute.Tensor,  # (dim, K)          conv taps
+    mBias: cute.Tensor,  # (dim,)            conv bias (zeros when conv_bias=False)
+    mOut: cute.Tensor,  # (T_total, dim)    C_gate-gated conv output
+    mState: cute.Tensor,  # (slots, dim, K-1) static, mutated
+    mQsl: cute.Tensor,  # (B+1,) int32      cumulative per-request token offsets
+    mSlot: cute.Tensor,  # (B,) int64        per-request state-slot index
+    mHasInit: cute.Tensor,  # (B,) int          1 if conv_state holds a real prefix
+    dim: cutlass.Int32,
+    SLOTS: cutlass.Constexpr,
+    K: cutlass.Constexpr,
+    CHUNK: cutlass.Constexpr,
+    BLOCK_D: cutlass.Constexpr,
+):
+    """One thread per channel, gridded over (d-tile, token-chunk, request) for varlen
+    prefill.
+
+    Each thread streams CHUNK tokens of one request for its channel, keeping the K-1
+    causal window of `Bx = B_gate * x` in registers; per-token reads coalesce across
+    the warp (dim contiguous). The window is seeded from conv_state when has_initial
+    (chunked prefill / carried prefix) else zero, and the chunk holding the request's
+    last token writes the final window back as the new state. mProj columns are
+    [0:dim)=B_gate, [dim:2dim)=C_gate, [2dim:3dim)=x. Out-of-range slots are skipped.
+    """
+    tidx, _, _ = cute.arch.thread_idx()  # channel within the d-tile
+    bdx, bc, bb = cute.arch.block_idx()  # d-tile, token-chunk, request
+    d = bdx * BLOCK_D + tidx
+    cute.arch.griddepcontrol_wait()
+    s = mQsl[bb]
+    e = mQsl[bb + 1]
+    treq = e - s
+    c0 = bc * CHUNK  # first token of this chunk within the request
+    slot = mSlot[bb]
+    if d < dim and c0 < treq and slot >= 0 and slot < SLOTS:
+        mss = mState[slot, None, None]  # (dim, K-1) at int64 slot offset
+        has_init = mHasInit[bb]
+        wv = cute.make_rmem_tensor(K, cutlass.Float32)
+        for k in cutlass.range_constexpr(K):
+            wv[k] = mW[d, k].to(cutlass.Float32)
+        bias = mBias[d].to(cutlass.Float32)
+        win = cute.make_rmem_tensor(K - 1, cutlass.Float32)
+        for j in cutlass.range_constexpr(K - 1):
+            r = c0 - (K - 1) + j  # req-token index for window slot j (oldest first)
+            hv = cutlass.Float32(0.0)
+            if r >= 0:
+                hv = mProj[s + r, d].to(cutlass.Float32) * mProj[s + r, 2 * dim + d].to(
+                    cutlass.Float32
+                )  # B_gate*x
+            elif has_init != 0:
+                hv = mss[d, (K - 1) + r].to(
+                    cutlass.Float32
+                )  # before request -> initial state
+            win[j] = hv
+        cend = c0 + CHUNK
+        if cend > treq:
+            cend = treq
+        t = c0
+        while t < cend:
+            bxv = mProj[s + t, d].to(cutlass.Float32) * mProj[s + t, 2 * dim + d].to(
+                cutlass.Float32
+            )  # B_gate*x
+            cgate = mProj[s + t, dim + d].to(cutlass.Float32)
+            acc = bias
+            for j in cutlass.range_constexpr(K - 1):
+                acc = acc + win[j] * wv[j]
+            acc = acc + bxv * wv[K - 1]
+            mOut[s + t, d] = (acc * cgate).to(mOut.element_type)
+            for j in cutlass.range_constexpr(K - 2):
+                win[j] = win[j + 1]
+            win[K - 2] = bxv
+            t = t + 1
+        if cend == treq:
+            for j in cutlass.range_constexpr(K - 1):
+                mss[d, j] = win[j].to(mState.element_type)
+    cute.arch.griddepcontrol_launch_dependents()
+
+
+@cute.jit
+def _prefill_host(
+    mProj,
+    mW,
+    mBias,
+    mOut,
+    mState,
+    mQsl,
+    mSlot,
+    mHasInit,
+    dim: cutlass.Int32,
+    n_chunks: cutlass.Int32,
+    B: cutlass.Int32,
+    SLOTS: cutlass.Constexpr,
+    K: cutlass.Constexpr,
+    CHUNK: cutlass.Constexpr,
+    BLOCK_D: cutlass.Constexpr,
+    stream: cuda.CUstream,
+):
+    grid_d = (dim + BLOCK_D - 1) // BLOCK_D
+    _prefill_kernel(
+        mProj,
+        mW,
+        mBias,
+        mOut,
+        mState,
+        mQsl,
+        mSlot,
+        mHasInit,
+        dim,
+        SLOTS,
+        K,
+        CHUNK,
+        BLOCK_D,
+    ).launch(
+        grid=[grid_d, n_chunks, B], block=[BLOCK_D, 1, 1], stream=stream, use_pdl=True

detail.body:
## Summary

Add native text generation for the LFM3 family in SGLang.

| Model | Inputs | Output |
| --- | --- | --- |
| LFM3 | Text | Text |
| LFM3-VL | Text, images, video | Text |
| LFM3-Audio | Text, audio | Text |
| LFM3-Omni | Text, images, audio, video, including video soundtracks | Text |

Uses stock Transformers with `--trust-remote-code` to load the checkpoint-provided configs and processors.

## Implementation

- Shared LFM3 backbone with gated short convolutions, full/sliding-window attention, and SGLang's hybrid cache integration. Includes CuTe DSL convolution kernels and a PyTorch fallback.
- Vision and audio encoders, projectors, and checkpoint loading. Omni reuses these components and the text backbone.
- Multimodal preprocessing uses the checkpoint's Transformers processors and chat template. Omni supports mixed inputs and video/audio interleaving.
- FlashInfer defaults to paged prefill for correct sliding-window attention.

## Usage

Choose a checkpoint for the input modalities you need:

| Model | Checkpoint |
| --- | --- |
| Text | [LiquidAI/LFM3-1.7B](https://huggingface.co/LiquidAI/LFM3-1.7B) |
| Vision | [LiquidAI/LFM3-VL-2B](https://huggingface.co/LiquidAI/LFM3-VL-2B) |
| Audio | [LiquidAI/LFM3-Audio-2B](https://huggingface.co/LiquidAI/LFM3-Audio-2B) |
| Omni | [LiquidAI/LFM3-Omni-2B](https://huggingface.co/LiquidAI/LFM3-Omni-2B) |

For example, launch Omni:

```bash
sglang serve \
  --model-path LiquidAI/LFM3-Omni-2B \
  --trust-remote-code \
  --reasoning-parser auto --tool-call-parser auto \
  --served-model-name lfm3 \
  --port 30000
```

Send requests through `/v1/chat/completions`. This client works with each model; select supported content below. Replace example media URLs with files reachable by the server.

```python
import base64
from pathlib import Path
from openai import OpenAI

client = OpenAI(base_url="http://localhost:30000/v1", api_key="EMPTY")

def ask(content, **kwargs):
    response = client.chat.completions.create(
        model="lfm3",
        messages=[{"role": "user", "content": content}],
        temperature=0,
        max_tokens=256,
        **kwargs,
    )
    print(response.choices[0].message.content)

# Text
ask("What is the capital of Poland?")

# Image
image = {"type": "image_url", "image_url": {"url": "https://your-host/image.jpg"}}
ask([image, {"type": "text", "text": "Describe this image."}])

# Video
video = {"type": "video_url", "video_url": {"url": "https://your-host/video.mp4"}}
ask([video, {"type": "text", "text": "Describe this video."}])

# Audio
encoded = base64.b64encode(Path("question.wav").read_bytes()).decode("ascii")
audio = {"type": "input_audio", "input_audio": {"data": encoded, "format": "wav"}}
ask([audio, {"type": "text", "text": "Answer the spoken question in text."}])

# Omni: image + spoken question
ask([image, audio])

# Omni: video with its soundtrack
ask(
    [video, {"type": "text", "text": "Summarize what happens and what is said."}],
    extra_body={"use_audio_in_video": True},
)
```

For transcription, launch LFM3-Audio and call the existing endpoint:

```bash
curl http://localhost:30000/v1/audio/transcriptions \
  -F model=lfm3 -F file=@question.wav
```

## Validation

Validation below was run on development checkpoints. FP16, TP1, H100, FlashInfer against Transformers; serving uses stock Transformers 5.19.0 with `--trust-remote-code`.

| Suite | Prefill/decode checks | ROUGE-L |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Text | 4/4 | 4/4 |
| Vision | 16/16 | 14/16 |
| Audio → text | 5/5 | 5/5 |
| Omni → text | 22/22 | 20/22 |

All 211 targeted CPU tests and 259 subtests passed. Live tool calling with both parsers set to `auto` and startup rejection probes passed. Vision ROUGE compares raw output with parsing disabled.

Triton also passed all 20 text/vision prefill and decode checks in FP16 on H100 with 1,024-token prefill chunks, including a long prompt beyond the 256-token sliding window. All generated outputs matched the FlashInfer run; the same two vision ROUGE failures remained. Audio and Omni were not tested with Triton.

Additional coverage: BF16 Omni smoke tests on H100; independent BF16 text/VL validation on H200, including TP2 text.
